page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m1.4xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The compute configuration provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with exactly 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators and has no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for system and data persistence.

Network connectivity is provisioned with a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth, facilitating consistent data exchange within the cloud environment. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring an elastic IP or NAT configuration for external internet connectivity. The resource balance prioritizes dedicated core density over memory volume, delivering computational throughput while avoiding expenditures on idle memory. The operational tradeoff is the constrained memory footprint of 1.0 GB per thread, which is incompatible with large in-memory databases or caching layers.

Given its compute-heavy profile, the server is suitable for highly parallel tasks with modest per-thread memory demands. Target workloads include batch data processing, distributed task workers, continuous integration build jobs, media transcoding pipelines, and compute-focused microservice architectures.
